title: Concerns of people of Siang Valley over dam project to be addressed through dialogue: Amit Shah

ai.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah assured Siang Valley residents that concerns over the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project would be addressed through dialogue, emphasizing the project's national importance and strategic value for Arunachal Pradesh while promising rehabilitation packages and cultural respect.

facts.claim: Union Home Minister Amit Shah assured the people of Siang Valley that their concerns would be addressed through dialogue
facts.quote: I want to assure my brothers and sisters from Siang that we will find a way forward through positive dialogue... You need not worry about it.

facts.claim: The proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project is of national importance and crucial for Arunachal Pradesh’s development and strategic interests
facts.quote: Asserting that the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) is of national importance and crucial for Arunachal Pradesh’s development and strategic interests

facts.claim: The government would provide 'one of the country’s most attractive' rehabilitation and resettlement packages
facts.quote: Shah also assured people that the government would provide 'one of the country’s most attractive' rehabilitation and resettlement packages for those affected by the proposed project.

facts.claim: The project is considered strategically important by the Centre, particularly in view of China’s plans to develop a massive hydropower project on the upper reaches of the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet
facts.quote: The project, proposed on the Siang River, is considered strategically important by the Centre, particularly in view of China’s plans to develop a massive hydropower project on the upper reaches of the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet, which enters India as the Siang before flowing into Assam as the Brahmaputra.

ai.background_note: Union Home Minister Amit Shah visited Arunachal Pradesh to address Siang Valley concerns over the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, emphasizing dialogue and rehabilitation packages amid indigenous opposition.
